s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic systemic illness with fever, weight loss, and localized inflammatory lesions
salient_findings: Progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and dry cough
Painful nonhealing ulcer on the right hallux
Chronic lower back pain with tenderness over the thoracic spine
Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation on biopsy of the toe ulcer
Bilateral reticular-nodular opacities on chest radiograph
key_facts: Negative sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics
No lymphadenopathy or edema on examination
Negative ANA, anti-dsDNA, ANCA, HIV, hepatitis B and C, and syphilis serologies
3+ leukocytes and 3+ red blood cells on urine dipstick
Induced sputum trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid on culture
Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus on biopsy of the toe ulcer
Contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection on MRI of the spine

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Induced sputum trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert, MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid on culture, and necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus on biopsy of the toe ulcer

shortlist.label: Spinal brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection on MRI of the spine, and chronic back pain

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis due to Mycobacterium tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic back pain, and contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection on MRI of the spine

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, and chronic systemic illness with fever, weight loss, and localized inflammatory lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and test results, including a 2-year history of progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough, along with the presence of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus on biopsy of the toe ulcer and a trace positive MTB on GeneXpert, are consistent with tuberculosis. The patient's MTB culture was also sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid, which further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spondylitis
rejected.why: While the patient does have contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection on MRI of the spine, this is more likely a complication of tuberculosis rather than the primary diagnosis.
